### Quickstart with Peekaboo CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/peekaboo/SKILL.md

Basic commands to get started with Peekaboo, including checking permissions, listing applications, taking a screenshot, clicking an element, and typing text.

```bash
peekaboo permissions
peekaboo list apps --json
peekaboo see --annotate --path /tmp/peekaboo-see.png
peekaboo click --on B1
peekaboo type "Hello" --return
```

--------------------------------

### PostgreSQL State Setup Advisory and Docker Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/SKILL.md

This advisory provides instructions for configuring PostgreSQL state, including setting the connection URL and a quick Docker setup example for a local PostgreSQL instance.

```text
⚠️  PostgreSQL state requires a connection URL.

To configure:
1. Set up a PostgreSQL database (Docker, local, or cloud)
2. Add connection string to .prose/.env:

   echo "OPENPROSE_POSTGRES_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/prose" >> .prose/.env

Quick Docker setup:
   docker run -d --name prose-pg -e POSTGRES_DB=prose -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
   echo "OPENPROSE_POSTGRES_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/prose" >> .prose/.env

See state/postgres.md for detailed setup options.
```

--------------------------------

### OpenClaw Development Loop Setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/README.md

Use these commands to clone the OpenClaw repository, install dependencies, perform initial setup, optionally prebuild the Control UI, and start the gateway in watch mode for development.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
cd openclaw

pnpm install

# First run only (or after resetting local OpenClaw config/workspace)
pnpm openclaw setup

# Optional: prebuild Control UI before first startup
pnpm ui:build

# Dev loop (auto-reload on source/config changes)
pnpm gateway:watch
```

--------------------------------

### Examples for Installing OpenClaw Hook Packs

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/hooks.md

These examples demonstrate installing hook packs from a local directory, a local archive, an npm package, and linking a local directory.

```bash
# Local directory
openclaw plugins install ./my-hook-pack

# Local archive
openclaw plugins install ./my-hook-pack.zip

# NPM package
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/my-hook-pack

# Link a local directory without copying
openclaw plugins install -l ./my-hook-pack
```

### wizard.start

```APIDOC
## RPC Method: wizard.start

### Description
This method initiates the onboarding wizard process. It exposes the wizard functionality over the WebSocket RPC interface, allowing clients to begin the guided setup.

### Method Name
wizard.start

### Parameters
None explicitly mentioned.

### Returns
None explicitly mentioned.
```

### Quick Start with swabble CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/apps/swabble/README.md

Commands to install dependencies, build, set up configuration, run the daemon, test hooks, and transcribe audio files using the swabble command-line interface.

```bash
# Install deps
brew install swiftformat swiftlint

# Build
swift build

# Write default config (~/.config/swabble/config.json)
swift run swabble setup

# Run foreground daemon
swift run swabble serve

# Test your hook
swift run swabble test-hook "hello world"

# Transcribe a file to SRT
swift run swabble transcribe /path/to/audio.m4a --format srt --output out.srt
```

### Example `package.json` with OpenClaw Channel Metadata

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/architecture-internals.md

This JSON snippet illustrates how a plugin's `package.json` uses the `openclaw.channel` and `openclaw.install` fields to define metadata for channel discovery, setup, and installation hints. It includes details like channel ID, labels, documentation paths, and npm/local installation specifications.

```json
{
  "name": "@openclaw/nextcloud-talk",
  "openclaw": {
    "extensions": ["./index.ts"],
    "channel": {
      "id": "nextcloud-talk",
      "label": "Nextcloud Talk",
      "selectionLabel": "Nextcloud Talk (self-hosted)",
      "docsPath": "/channels/nextcloud-talk",
      "docsLabel": "nextcloud-talk",
      "blurb": "Self-hosted chat via Nextcloud Talk webhook bots.",
      "order": 65,
      "aliases": ["nc-talk", "nc"]
    },
    "install": {
      "npmSpec": "@openclaw/nextcloud-talk",
      "localPath": "<bundled-plugin-local-path>",
      "defaultChoice": "npm"
    }
  }
}
```

### Example Project Environment File

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/scripts/clawdock/README.md

Shows a typical `<project>/.env` file, configuring Docker infrastructure settings like image name, ports, and gateway token.

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw
OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw/workspace
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18789
OPENCLAW_BRIDGE_PORT=18790
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_BIND=lan
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<generated-by-docker-setup>
OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw-auth-profile-secrets
OPENCLAW_IMAGE=openclaw:local
```

### Install Homebrew on Linux

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq-first-run.md

Provides commands to install Homebrew (Linuxbrew) and configure its shell environment, followed by an example of installing a formula.

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
echo 'eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> ~/.profile
eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
brew install <formula>
```

### AI-Evaluated Discretion Condition Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/compiler.md

This example demonstrates using discretion markers (`**...**`) for AI-evaluated conditions to guide session execution based on code analysis.

```prose
let analysis = session "Analyze the codebase"

if **the code has security vulnerabilities**:
  session "Fix security issues immediately"
    context: analysis
elif **the code has performance issues**:
  session "Optimize performance bottlenecks"
    context: analysis
else:
  session "Proceed with normal review"
    context: analysis
```

### Example JSON Input for Install Policy Executable

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skills-config.md

This JSON object is passed to the policy executable via stdin, providing details about the installation request, target, and source.

```json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "openclawVersion": "2026.6.1",
  "targetType": "skill",
  "targetName": "weather",
  "sourcePath": "/var/folders/.../openclaw-skill-clawhub/root",
  "sourcePathKind": "directory",
  "source": {
    "kind": "clawhub",
    "authority": "openclaw",
    "mutable": false,
    "network": true
  },
  "origin": {
    "type": "clawhub",
    "registry": "https://clawhub.openclaw.ai",
    "slug": "weather",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "request": {
    "kind": "skill-install",
    "mode": "install",
    "requestedSpecifier": "clawhub:weather@1.0.0"
  },
  "skill": {
    "installId": "clawhub"
  }
}
```

```shell
node --import tsx scripts/bench-gateway-restart.ts --json
```

### Re-run Docker Setup for Existing Installs

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/docker.md

This snippet reloads existing Docker environment variables and re-runs the setup script, ensuring the OPENCLAW_HOME_VOLUME is correctly configured for persistent storage.

```bash
set -a
. ./.env
set +a
export OPENCLAW_HOME_VOLUME="${OPENCLAW_HOME_VOLUME:-openclaw_home}"
./scripts/docker/setup.sh
```

### Set Up Multiple Gateways with Default and Named Profiles

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/multiple-gateways.md

These commands demonstrate how to initialize and run a main Gateway using the default profile and an additional Gateway with a custom named profile and unique port.

```bash

openclaw setup
openclaw gateway --port 18789
```

```bash
# extra gateway
openclaw --profile ops setup
openclaw --profile ops gateway --port 19789
```

### Shelley Agent Prompt for OpenClaw Installation

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/exe-dev.md

Use this prompt with exe.dev's Shelley agent to automatically install and configure OpenClaw Gateway on a VM, including Nginx setup for WebSocket support.

```text
Set up OpenClaw (https://docs.openclaw.ai/install) on this VM. Use the non-interactive and accept-risk flags for openclaw onboarding. Add the supplied auth or token as needed. Configure nginx to forward from the default port 18789 to the root location on the default enabled site config, making sure to enable Websocket support. Pairing is done by "openclaw devices list" and "openclaw devices approve <request id>". Make sure the dashboard shows that OpenClaw's health is OK. exe.dev handles forwarding from port 8000 to port 80/443 and HTTPS for us, so the final "reachable" should be <vm-name>.exe.xyz, without port specification.
```
